data.title: Granuloma annulare — viva
data.summary: Granulomatous disorders · 8 viva questions with answers
data.body:
_Viva questions for the case: **Granuloma annulare** (Granulomatous disorders)_

**Q1. What is granuloma annulare (GA)?**
- Benign, usually self-limiting, non-infectious granulomatous dermatosis with annular arrangement of smooth papules; children and young adults (localised), middle-aged women (generalised)

**Q2. Clinical variants.**
- Localised (commonest — dorsa of hands/feet, fingers, ankles; skin-coloured to pink beaded papules in a ring without scale; central skin normal or slightly violaceous)
- Generalised/disseminated (≥10 lesions on trunk and limbs; adults; associations — diabetes, dyslipidaemia, thyroid disease, HIV, malignancy (lymphoma) in some; chronic)
- Subcutaneous (deep nodules on shins, scalp, hands of children — 'pseudo-rheumatoid nodules')
- Perforating (umbilicated papules with central crust — hands)
- Patch/macular (erythematous patches — 'interstitial GA'), micropapular, actinic (photo-exposed — annular elastolytic giant cell granuloma), drug-induced (TNF inhibitors, allopurinol, ACE inhibitors)

**Q3. Pathogenesis.**
- Unknown — delayed-type hypersensitivity reaction to an unknown antigen with collagen degeneration (necrobiosis) and mucin; triggers: insect bites, trauma, tuberculin test, vaccines, sun, viral infections, drugs; Th1 cells, TNF-α, JAK-STAT signalling (basis for JAK inhibitors)

**Q4. Histopathology.**
- Palisading granuloma: central zone of altered (necrobiotic) collagen with abundant mucin surrounded by palisading histiocytes and lymphocytes in upper/mid dermis
- Interstitial pattern: histiocytes scattered between collagen bundles with mucin ('busy dermis')
- Mucin (Alcian blue/colloidal iron) differentiates from necrobiosis lipoidica (little mucin, layered 'cake' pattern, plasma cells) and rheumatoid nodule (fibrinoid necrosis, deeper)

**Q5. Differential diagnosis of annular plaques.**
- Tinea corporis (scaly active edge, KOH), annular lichen planus (violaceous, Wickham's striae), tuberculoid/borderline-tuberculoid leprosy (anaesthesia, nerve), sarcoidosis (annular), necrobiosis lipoidica (shins, yellow atrophic), erythema annulare centrifugum (trailing scale), SCLE, secondary syphilis (annular), mycosis fungoides, actinic GA, porokeratosis (keratotic ridge)

**Q6. Investigations.**
- Clinical ± biopsy; in generalised GA: blood sugar/HbA1c, lipid profile, thyroid function, HIV, hepatitis; consider malignancy screen if atypical in elderly

**Q7. Treatment.**
- Localised: reassurance (50% resolve within 2 years), potent topical steroid under occlusion, intralesional triamcinolone (2.5–5 mg/ml), cryotherapy, tacrolimus; 'biopsy-induced resolution' is described
- Generalised: phototherapy (PUVA, NB-UVB, UVA1), hydroxychloroquine, dapsone, isotretinoin, doxycycline/minocycline + rifampicin + ofloxacin ('ROM' monthly combination), pentoxifylline, methotrexate, TNF inhibitors (paradoxical GA reported too), JAK inhibitors (tofacitinib) for refractory
- Treat associated diabetes/dyslipidaemia

**Q8. Prognosis.**
- Localised GA resolves spontaneously in ~50% within 2 years without scars but recurs in ~40% (often at same site); generalised GA more chronic and resistant

## Quick spotter facts
- Ring of smooth skin-coloured beaded papules on dorsa of hands, no scale — GA
- Palisading granuloma with mucin

_Sources: Previous-year PG question papers (Sahana P Raju, Solved Papers Dermatology); IADVL Textbook of Dermatology 5e (Non-infectious granulomas). Answers written in our own words; check with your teachers' preferences._
